analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is a lifetime/order bug: removeSession() schedules removeSessionCallback as a delayed callback that calls UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup() and frees the session entry, but pending repeated subscription publish callbacks are not unregistered/cancelled before that free. During shutdown, processDelayedCallbacks executes the delayed free, and then a stale publish/subscription callback path reaches UA_Subscription_answerPublishRequestsNoSubscription() with a dangling UA_Session*, causing heap-use-after-free when accessing session fields (e.g., serverSubscriptions / channel). The crash is observed in ua_subscription.c, but the missing teardown ordering is in session removal/cleanup logic.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires creating a session (via fuzzed binary CreateSession flow), establishing state that leaves subscription/publish-related callbacks or queued publish handling associated with that session, then driving shutdown (harness calls UA_Server_run_shutdown). In single-threaded delayed-callback processing, the session memory is freed by removeSessionCallback, yet later callback execution still uses the freed session pointer in UA_Subscription_answerPublishRequestsNoSubscription, producing UAF.
